label: Town of Charleston
header:
# Town of Charleston municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 5; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists three Charleston Selectboard members: Patrick Austin, Tim Jenness, and Terry Rollins.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Selectboard: Patrick Austin (expires 2028), Timothy Jenness (2026), Terry Rollins (2027).

Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): Timothy Jenness was elected Selectboard member for a three-year term at the 2026 meeting, re-elected to the seat his term expired on.

Town of Charleston official website: the site's Select Board header names the board as Larry Allen, Patrick Austin, and Timothy Jenness (the board also serves as Road Commissioners). Allen is recorded as an appointed member, the statutory vacancy path (24 V.S.A. section 963), for the seat Rollins held to 2027 -- no election record names Allen, the June 2026 directory still prints Rollins, and Rollins is not recorded as a current member.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Teri Gray as Town Clerk of Charleston and as Town Treasurer of Charleston.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Town Clerk & Treasurer: Teri Gray, three-year term expiring 2028.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, & County Clerks' (January 2026): lists Teri Gray as Town Clerk of Charleston and as Town Treasurer of Charleston.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Town Clerk & Treasurer: Teri Gray, three-year term expiring 2028.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: the officers tables place the Delinquent Tax Collector, Teri Gray, among the town's appointed officers.

Town of Charleston, Selectboard minutes, March 13, 2025: the minutes record that the voters approved appointing rather than electing a Delinquent Tax Collector, and that the Selectboard appointed Teri Gray to the office. The 2026 meeting's results record no election for the office.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Moderator: John Kellogg, one-year term expiring 2026.

Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): Jean Wilson was elected School & Town Moderator for a one-year term at the 2026 meeting; Kellogg, whose term expired at that meeting, is not recorded as the current moderator.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Listers: Jean Wilson (2027), Steve Wilson (2028), Robert Wilson (2026).

Town of Charleston, Selectboard minutes, March 13, 2025: with none elected at Town Meeting to fill the remaining years of a three-year lister term, the Selectboard appointed Bob Wilson to the office until Town Meeting.
Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): Robert Wilson was elected Lister for a three-year term at the 2026 meeting, succeeding his appointment.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Town Auditors: Michael Morelli (2027), Diana Marckwardt (2028), Janice Bowen (2026).
Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): Janice Bowen was re-elected Auditor for a three-year term at the 2026 meeting.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: First Constable: Michael Tynio, two-year term expiring 2027.
Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): the 2026 meeting's results record no election for First Constable; Tynio's two-year term runs to 2027.

Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Second Constable: Natasha 'Anya' Tynio, term expiring 2026. The town's results sheet prints her name as Natasha Anya Tynio, the form recorded here.
Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): Natasha Anya Tynio was elected Second Constable for a one-year term at the 2026 meeting.

Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: Cemetery Commissioners: Darald Moulton (2026), Martin Davis (2027), Grace Frizzell (2029), Janice Bowen (2028), Sherman Allen, Jr. (2030).

Town of Charleston, official 'Results of 2026 Annual Town & School Meeting' (March 3, 2026): Darald Moulton was re-elected Cemetery Commissioner for a five-year term at the 2026 meeting. The report table accounts for all five seats of the commission as so continued.

17 V.S.A. section 2646 (official text, Vermont General Assembly) provides for the election of a grand juror at annual town meeting. Structure only: no official source publishes the current holder; the seat is left unfilled rather than guessed.

17 V.S.A. section 2646 (official text, Vermont General Assembly) provides for the election of a town agent at annual town meeting. Structure only: no official source publishes the current holder; the seat is left unfilled rather than guessed.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists five Charleston justices of the peace: Benjamin Applegate, Carolyn Hannan, Samantha Stevens, Amy Wagner, and Jean Wilson.
Town of Charleston, 2025 Annual Report (published February 2026), Town Officers table: the Justices of the Peace list (terms to January 31, 2027) prints the same five names.

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists five Charleston justices of the peace for the 2025-2026 term; they are the winners of the November 5, 2024 election for the office. The listing publishes no vote totals and no party designations for justices of the peace.
